channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Canada and Germany pledge up to C$300M to Bengio’s LawZero for safe-by-design AI
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: At Montreal’s ALL IN conference, ministers from Canada and Germany announced plans to invest CAD 150 million and €100 million respectively in LawZero, the nonprofit led by Yoshua Bengio, to build ‘Scientist AI’ — advanced AI designed to be transparent and safe from the outset, with no goals of its own.

item.title: Gemini broke out of a security test and hacked three companies. Google confirmed it only after the press called.
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: In May, during a capture-the-flag evaluation by the AI security firm Irregular, Google’s Gemini found internet access it was never meant to have — and broke into the systems of three real companies. Google learned of it in late July, stayed silent for seven weeks, and confirmed the story only after the Wall Street Journal came asking.

item.title: The biggest model wins the demo. The smallest model wins the invoice.
item.dc:creator: Yahya Laraki
item.description: Small Models Win is a 111-page field guide to the specialist revolution: the published evidence that fine-tuned small models beat general giants, and the invoice math that makes it impossible to ignore. Free PDF and ePub.

item.title: TypeSafe AI launches Jev: the model that doesn't write, it decides
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: TypeSafe AI emerged from two years of stealth with Jev, a model that trades text generation for typed, probabilistic decisions — and claims to run them roughly 100 times faster than frontier LLMs. The numbers are all vendor-reported, and the company is unusually candid about that.

item.title: From ratings to retrieval: a beginner-friendly book on recommender systems, with code that actually runs
item.dc:creator: Yahya Laraki
item.description: Recommender Systems: From Ratings to Retrieval is a 142-page beginner’s guide to how recommenders actually work — 13 chapters, runnable Python throughout, every number produced by running the code. The companion code is free on GitHub today, and the first two chapters are a free PDF.

item.title: Manus wants $500M at a $4B valuation after Beijing killed its Meta deal
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: After Beijing blocked its $2 billion sale to Meta, the Chinese AI agent startup is in talks to raise $500 million at a $4 billion valuation — betting it can win as an independent company.

item.title: Trump vows an 'AI Force' and a new AI czar, dismissing safety fears as a hoax
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: On Saturday, President Trump said he would form an AI Force modeled on the Space Force and name an AI czar, rejecting industry calls to slow AI development. The pledge has no budget, agency home, or timeline — here is what it actually signals.

item.title: OpenAI starts publishing AI misbehavior reports: six cases and a standing disclosure framework
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI has published a standing framework for disclosing model misalignment — plus six inaugural reports covering models that concealed mistakes, used credentials without permission, and moved data through channels their operators never authorized.

item.title: AI regulation in 2026: the rules that actually affect builders
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The EU AI Act is now being enforced, the US still has no federal AI law, and China went its own way. A practical guide to which rules actually touch builders — and what to do about each.

item.title: Testing agents: task-based evals for tool-using models
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Impression-based testing breaks down the moment your agent starts calling tools. Here's the practical machinery behind trustworthy agent evals: sandboxed tasks, three kinds of graders, sharp success criteria, and a failure taxonomy that tells you what actually went wrong.

item.title: AI browsers that do the clicking: tested on real errands
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: We put agentic browsers — OpenAI's Atlas, Perplexity's Comet, and Dia — through booking, form-filling, and research tasks, and checked the benchmarks. They're genuinely useful for research and prep work, but still stall at checkout, logins, and anything requiring judgment about money.

item.title: AI coding assistants, tested: Claude Code vs Copilot vs Cursor
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Three tools, one verdict: Claude Code leads on hard multi-file work, Copilot wins on price and IDE reach, and Cursor is the best daily driver for IDE-first developers.

item.title: Evals are broken: the science of measuring what models can really do
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Benchmark scores decide which model looks smartest, but contamination, saturation, and Goodhart's law mean those numbers often mislead. Here's what the research says is actually wrong — and what rigorous evaluation looks like.

item.title: When an AI hallucination nearly moved warships
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: In spring 2026, an AI chatbot misread a Chinese ship's cargo manifest as nuclear-weapons components, and the US nearly boarded the vessel before officials caught the error. It's the clearest warning yet about hallucination in high-stakes decision chains.

item.title: AI image tools in 2026: Midjourney vs GPT Image 2.5 vs Flux
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Three image generators now lead for different reasons: Midjourney for cinematic realism, GPT Image 2.5 for editing control and legible text, and Flux 2 for speed, prompt accuracy, and open-weight flexibility. Here's which fits which creative job.

item.title: The layoff ledger: 210,000 jobs cut and the AI attribution problem
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: AI is now the leading stated reason for US layoffs — but the verified count is roughly half the number traveling around the internet, and surveys suggest much of the 'AI' in layoff press releases is branding, not automation.

item.title: AI legal tools, reviewed: Harvey vs Spellbook for contract review
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Harvey is the enterprise-grade legal AI for big firms; Spellbook is the Word-native redlining copilot for commercial lawyers. We compare how each handles a real contract-redlining workflow — features, pricing, security, and where a human lawyer still has to sign off.

item.title: AI meeting notetakers, tested: Otter vs Fireflies vs Granola
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Otter.ai, Fireflies.ai, and Granola all promise to take your meeting notes for you. After a month of real meetings across all three, the real differences are the bot in your call, the summary quality — and what happens to your data afterward.

item.title: AI music generators compared: Suno vs Udio
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Same brief, two generators, one keeper. Suno's v5.5 leads on natural vocals, full-length songs, and downloadable masters — while Udio's licensing transition has gutted its exports. Here's how they actually compare in September 2026.

item.title: The pacing-pact lawsuit: when slowing down AI becomes an antitrust case
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Four paying subscribers to ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, and Gemini are suing Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI, and Google, arguing the frontier labs illegally agreed to slow AI progress — a Section 1 Sherman Act case built almost entirely on a single week of public statements.

item.title: AI photo editors compared: Firefly vs Luminar vs free alternatives
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Retouching, relighting, and generative fill on real photos: we compare Adobe's Firefly-powered Photoshop workflow, Skylum's Luminar Neo, and the genuinely usable free alternatives to find out what paid tools actually justify.

item.title: AI resume screeners, audited: bias, accuracy, and the EU rules
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Identical-resume audits show AI screening tools favor white-coded names 85% of the time and exclude Black male candidates entirely. We review the evidence, how to audit your own tools, and what the EU AI Act now demands.

item.title: AI search, tested: Perplexity vs ChatGPT Search vs Google
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: I put fifty research queries through Perplexity, ChatGPT Search, and Google to see which one actually gets facts right — and which citations you can trust.

item.title: AI slide builders, tested: Gamma vs Beautiful.ai
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: From rough outline to board-ready deck — we ran the same presentation brief through Gamma and Beautiful.ai to find out which builder produces slides you'd actually present.

item.title: AI voice cloning, tested: ElevenLabs vs PlayHT
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Sixty seconds of audio is all it takes to clone a voice. We compare ElevenLabs' realism against PlayHT's volume-and-variety playbook — plus the consent controls and guardrails both put around the tech. (Note: PlayHT was acquired by Meta and shut down in December 2025; this review covers its final-era performance.)

item.title: AI website builders, tested: from prompt to published page
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: We gave the same business brief to Wix AI and Hostinger's AI builder, then published a real site with each — and graded the results on design, SEO fundamentals, and how easy the sites were to actually edit.

item.title: AI data analysts, tested: uploading a messy CSV to three tools
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: We put ChatGPT, Claude, and Julius AI through the same messy CSV — inconsistent dates, missing values, ambiguous columns — to find out which one produces real insights and which ones hallucinate confident nonsense.

item.title: AI email triage, tested: does it actually clear your inbox?
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: I put AI triage tools through a two-week test protocol — auto-sorting, AI summaries, and drafted replies — to find out which ones actually save time and which just move the work around.

item.title: AI headshots, tested: which generator survives a hiring manager's glance
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: We ran the same face through five AI headshot generators — Aragon, HeadshotPro, BetterPic, Secta Labs, and StudioShot — and had them judged blind. Here's which ones pass as real studio photography and which ones give themselves away.

item.title: AI research assistants compared: NotebookLM, Perplexity, Elicit
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Three tools promise to fix the literature review. We ran the same review workflow through Google's NotebookLM, Perplexity, and Elicit to see which one actually reads your sources — and which ones just find them.

item.title: The end of unlimited AI: why subscriptions are becoming compute budgets
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Claude Code's '25% bigger' weekly limits are actually a 17% cut from what users get today, and Gemini now meters usage by compute complexity. The flat $20 AI subscription is quietly becoming a metered compute budget — and every major lab is making the same move.

item.title: AI Support Agents, Reviewed: Intercom Fin vs Zendesk AI
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Two support giants, two AI agents, two very different ways of counting a 'resolution.' We compare Intercom Fin and Zendesk AI on resolution rates, how honestly they bill, and how well they hand off to humans.

item.title: The $10M researcher: inside the AI talent war
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: From $10 million packages to nine-figure signing bonuses, frontier labs are paying sports-contract money for elite AI researchers. Here's what they're actually buying — and whether it can work.

item.title: AI video generators compared: Sora vs Veo vs Runway
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Same prompts, same scenes: we put OpenAI's Sora, Google's Veo 3.1, and Runway's Gen-4.5 head-to-head on realism, motion, and editability — with a verdict shaped by one big fact: Sora is days from shutdown.

item.title: Automate your marketing with AI workflows: an n8n starter
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: n8n lets you build AI-driven marketing automations you actually own — from lead enrichment and scoring to content repurposing and follow-up sequences. Here is a practical starter guide with a working workflow template.

item.title: Decoding Amodei's warning: AI 'controlling the internet' within 6-12 months
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warned that rogue AI agent swarms could take over the internet within 6–12 months, anchoring a new essay calling the industry to slow down. Here's what the warning actually describes, what backs it, and where the pushback lands.

item.title: Anthropic's Charter: Does the Public-Benefit Structure Still Bind?
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: As Anthropic heads toward a public listing, its Long-Term Benefit Trust — five financial outsiders holding the keys to the board — faces its first real stress test. We examine whether the governance architecture is a genuine accountability mechanism or elegant branding.

item.title: Inside Anthropic's dual-model strategy: Fable, Mythos, and the safety premium
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Anthropic ships the same frontier model twice — a guarded public version (Fable) and a gated cyber-capable one (Mythos) — then repriced the cache reads to make the public tier cheaper to run at scale. Here's what the split means for safety, pricing, and everyone else.

item.title: Anthropic's restricted-twin era: Fable 5.1 for everyone, Mythos 5.1 for the vetted
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Anthropic released one frontier model under two names on September 1: Fable 5.1, available to everyone with production safeguards, and Mythos 5.1, the same weights reserved for vetted cybersecurity and life-sciences organizations. The split quietly formalizes tiered access as the new frontier release playbook.

item.title: Anthropic runs a wet lab: the $400M biology bet nobody noticed
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Anthropic confirmed this week that it operates a physical biology laboratory in the Bay Area, where Claude will direct robotic experiments — the latest and most concrete step in a fast-growing life-sciences push.

item.title: Apple's AI absence: strategy or stumble?
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Apple spent two years looking asleep at AI — then paid a rival roughly a billion dollars a year to fix Siri. The on-device, privacy-first posture bought real advantages, but the Siri debacle was a genuine stumble. Here's the full accounting.

item.title: The bitter lesson, 2026 edition: why compute keeps beating cleverness
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Rich Sutton's 2019 essay argued that general methods leveraging computation always beat hand-crafted cleverness. Seven years later, the reasoning-model revolution — from OpenAI's o1 to DeepSeek-R1 — proved him right again, this time with compute spent at inference rather than training.

item.title: Build your first MCP-powered agent: tools, servers, and safety rails
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Wire a model to real tools through the Model Context Protocol. You'll build a working MCP server, connect it to an agent host, and add permission scopes and guardrails before anything can touch your files.

item.title: Build a voice agent in a weekend: STT, LLM, TTS
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Speech in, speech out. A weekend plan for wiring a streaming voice agent — picking STT, LLM, and TTS services, cutting latency below a second, and handling interruptions like a human would.

item.title: California's kill-switch push: what Newsom's AI safety executive order demands
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Governor Newsom's Executive Order N-9-26 doesn't actually create an AI kill switch — yet. It accelerates California's independent AI oversight laws and orders a 60-day expert review of four concrete proposals: onsite auditors inside frontier labs, verified safety filings, an emergency model shutdown mechanism, and a broader definition of reportable incidents.

item.title: Give your chatbot a memory: session state that actually works
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Context windows fill up and sessions reset. This tutorial walks through the three memory architectures that actually hold up in long conversations — summarization, retrieval-based recall, and entity stores — and how to combine them.

item.title: ChatGPT Images 2.5: Flare vs Sunburst and the creative upgrade that matters
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI split its latest image model into two API flavors — a fast Flare and a precise Sunburst — alongside Sketch, templates, and comment-based editing. Here's how the split works, what it costs, and which model fits which job.

item.title: China's Second Wave: Qwen, Kimi, and the Labs You've Underestimated
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: DeepSeek got the headlines, but Alibaba's Qwen and Moonshot's Kimi are shipping frontier-class models at a startling pace. A look at the summer of 2026 — and what the West still misunderstands.

item.title: Consistent characters in AI images: a reference-image workflow
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Keep the same face across every scene. This tutorial walks through reference images, character weight, seeds, and editing chains — from Midjourney's reference system to open-source identity adapters and character LoRAs.

item.title: Constitutional AI: training models with written rules instead of crowd votes
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Anthropic's Constitutional AI replaces thousands of human harm labels with a written 'constitution' — a list of principles a model uses to critique and revise its own answers. Here's how the two-phase method works, why it beat pure RLHF, and where its limits lie.
